wines.name: Rouge
wines.place: Vineyards high in the Bekaa Valley, about 1,000 m up, on gravel and limestone. The grapes cross the mountains to the cellars at Ghazir, north of Beirut.
wines.history: Gaston Hochar founded Musar in 1930. His son Serge kept making wine through the civil war of 1975 to 1990, when the harvest trucks crossed the front lines.
wines.contents: Each grape ferments and ages apart, about a year in French oak. The blend then rests in bottle for years before release.
wines.aromas: sour cherry, clove, cedar, dried fig

sketch.capsule: foil a little loose. Check the cork.

wines.name: Bandol Rouge
wines.place: Terraced hillsides near Le Castellet, above the Mediterranean, on clay and limestone. Sea air and hot sun ripen the late Mourvèdre.
wines.history: A wedding gift to Lucie and Lucien Peyraud in 1936. Lucien led the campaign for the Bandol appellation, with Mourvèdre at its heart.
wines.contents: Mostly Mourvèdre, aged about 18 months in large oak casks.
wines.aromas: black olive, leather, plum, dried thyme

wines.name: Von der Fels Riesling
wines.place: Flörsheim-Dalsheim, in the south of Rheinhessen, on limestone. The name means “from the rock”.
wines.history: The Kellers have made wine here since 1789. Klaus-Peter and Julia Keller helped turn Rheinhessen from a bulk-wine region into a home of great dry Riesling.
wines.contents: Young vines from the family’s best limestone vineyards, fermented dry.
wines.aromas: lime peel, wet slate, white peach

sketch.label: scuffed corner from the shop crate

wines.name: Vintage Port
wines.place: Steep schist terraces in the Douro Valley, including Quinta de Vargellas. The wine ages in the lodges at Vila Nova de Gaia.
wines.history: Founded in 1692, Taylor’s is one of the oldest port houses. It makes a vintage port only in the best years.
wines.contents: Trodden by foot in stone lagares. Grape spirit stops the fermentation and keeps the sweetness. Bottled unfiltered, so it throws a crust.

wines.name: Special Cuvée
wines.place: Aÿ, in the Marne valley. Pinot Noir from Aÿ and the Montagne de Reims leads the blend.
wines.history: Founded in 1829. Lily Bollinger ran the house from 1941 to 1971 and checked the vineyards by bicycle.
wines.contents: About 60% Pinot Noir. Part ferments in old oak, and the reserve wines age in magnums.

wines.name: Barbaresco
wines.place: The village of Barbaresco, in the Langhe hills of Piedmont, on chalky marl.
wines.history: The village priest brought the local growers together in 1958. In the best years they also bottle nine single-vineyard riservas.
wines.contents: Aged in large oak casks, the traditional way.

wines.name: Monte Bello
wines.place: Monte Bello Ridge in the Santa Cruz Mountains, 400 to 800 m up, on limestone above the Pacific fog.
wines.history: First planted in 1886. The 1971 Monte Bello placed fifth at the 1976 Paris tasting, and first at the rematch in 2006.
wines.contents: Mostly Cabernet Sauvignon. Wild yeast, then aged in American oak.

sketch.base: fine sediment. Decanted for an hour.

wines.name: Riesling
wines.place: Ribeauvillé, in Alsace, on slopes below the Vosges mountains.
wines.history: The Trimbach family has made wine since 1626. The house is known for bone-dry Riesling, and for Clos Sainte Hune.
wines.contents: Fermented fully dry and bottled young.

wines.name: Bandol Rosé
wines.place: The same seaside terraces near Le Castellet as the red.
wines.history: The Peyraud family estate since 1936, and a benchmark for Provence rosé.

wines.name: Cuvée de Réserve Blanc de Blancs
wines.place: Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, in the Côte des Blancs, on pure chalk.
wines.history: A family of growers in Le Mesnil. Rodolphe Péters makes the wines today.
wines.contents: Grand cru Chardonnay, blended with a perpetual reserve of older wines.
